analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily (18.11.2026)
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 103bps to 7340 (+7% YTD) and closed below its 200-day moving average on solid volumes. ETFs were nearly 36% of the tape. Focus is on tech regulation and Nvidia earnings.

Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8bn vs consensus $109.5bn, gross margin 74.9% vs 73.5%, and data center revenue $107.6bn vs $102.0bn. The stock traded +5% post market. Nebius and CoreWeave rose +11% and +9%.

Nvidia raised its CY27 revenue growth forecast to +75% from +70%. Management called Rubin the fastest product ramp in history, with $20bn of revenue in its first quarter. $227bn of buyback authorization remains.
Nvidia's support for neocloud customers totals $32bn of commitments. Financial commitments to customers and supply chain partners are $518bn. GS keeps a Buy rating with a $220 price target.

Nvidia's CFO said token prices fell 60% since May, which is accelerating token usage and compute demand. GPU rental prices are rising across generations. Hopper GPUs re-contracted at up to twice their original price, and B300 rates are up more than 60% since introduction. GS flags the GPU price point as important.

GS notes Nvidia demand is broadening beyond hyperscalers, compute is fully utilized, and an extra week in 4Q26 flatters sequential growth. China is optional upside to the guide. Memory is a major strategic constraint, and power and financing are becoming as important as chips.

Tech regulation headlines: new restrictions on China's access to high-end AI chips, a Reuters report that the Trump administration plans to press ahead with blocking imports of Chinese data center equipment, and a new Nvidia board committee on national security and export control.
US strikes on Iran hit a missile launch site on Qeshm Island. Tehran retaliated with air attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait.
Equinor detected an ongoing cyberattack. No indication data was stolen. GS points to its 16-stock cyber basket (Bloomberg ticker GSTMTCYB Index).
Nike's investor day was not enough. Management sees FY29 as the turning point and still expects sales to fall by high single digits in FY2027 as it cuts Sportswear and Jordan supply and resets China.

GS forecasts the S&P 500 at 8700 in 2027 (+17%). EPS growth is expected to slow from roughly 30% in 2026 to 18% in 2027. The base case holds the P/E near 18x as elevated rates and AI uncertainty offset earnings growth.
The WTI crack spread fell from roughly $69 to $38 since October, which GS says could mean less fuel pressure on inflation.

GS expects global growth of +2.8% in 2027 vs +2.7% in 2026, with downside risks from Iran, higher deficits and lower AI capex. GS expects 2 Fed hikes and 1 ECB hike from here, then cuts later in 2027.
The US ran a $404bn budget deficit in October, a record for the month and up $120bn (42% y/y). Interest cost was $115bn (+11%) against receipts of $369bn (-9% y/y).
GS sees near-term downside risk and elevated volatility in gold as the Fed hikes, but still targets $4650 by end-2027 on central bank purchases.
Market levels: US 10-year at 5.09%, Brent $92 (+52% YTD), gold $3790 (-12% YTD), Bitcoin $65k (-26% YTD), EUR/USD below 1.10. Kospi +2% with Samsung +2% and SK Hynix +4%.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Buy on a positive risk/reward after a beat on revenue, gross margin and data center, and a raised CY27 growth forecast.
Investor day did not convince. Management still expects FY2027 sales to fall by high single digits and sees FY29 as the turning point.

tension_points.bull_case: GS forecasts the S&P at 8700 (+17%) on EPS growth of 18% in 2027, with a solid economy and continued AI investment. If investors trust 2028 consensus and the P/E rises to 19x, the index reaches 9400.
tension_points.bear_case: If consensus EPS falls to the 30-year trend and the P/E drops to 17x, the S&P falls roughly 25% to about 5600. Elevated rates and AI uncertainty keep the P/E near 18x.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Consensus S&P EPS falling back to the 30-year trend with the P/E at the 30-year average of 17x.
